query: For phosphorus-containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys, what single intervention could improve glass-forming ability and the thermal stability of the amorphous state? Formulate one testable hypothesis that specifies the intervention without presupposing its class, the mechanism by which it would act, the predicted improvement relative to an otherwise comparable baseline, the conditions under which it should or should not work, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding phosphorus to high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys can improve their glass-forming ability and the thermal stability of the amorphous state.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy or compositionally complex alloys without phosphorus
generation.conditions: Alloy composition, cooling rate, and thermal treatment
generation.structural_mediator: Phosphorus-induced changes in alloy structure and properties
generation.mechanism: Phosphorus affecting the alloy's thermodynamic and kinetic properties, leading to improved glass-forming ability and thermal stability
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved glass-forming ability and thermal stability of the amorphous state
generation.baseline: High-entropy or compositionally complex alloys without phosphorus
generation.boundary: Alloy composition, cooling rate, and thermal treatment conditions
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanism by which phosphorus improves glass-forming ability and thermal stability is not well understood and requires further research

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys with and without phosphorus, and measure their glass-forming ability and thermal stability using techniques such as differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and X-ray diffraction (XRD)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of phosphorus does not improve the glass-forming ability and thermal stability of the alloy, the hypothesis is falsified
